requirements.requirement: node1 gets a routed interface addressed inside each VLAN (eth1 toward node2's VLAN, eth2 toward node3's VLAN)
requirements.summary: eth1 assigned 192.168.10.1/24 and eth2 assigned 192.168.20.1/24 on node1; verified live (cmd-418b59a1b1b24c06) and persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1-eth2 (cmd-a7a6df50d99b446f), and confirmed present again after node1's reboot (cmd-054b9bc895bd4458). The very first attempt (cmd-c955555330b149c7) returned rc=255 due to a duplicate-dev CLI error but the subsequent verification command shows both addresses correctly applied.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards traffic between the two VLAN interfaces (IPv4 forwarding enabled)
requirements.summary: net.ipv4.ip_forward, conf.all.forwarding, conf.eth1.forwarding, conf.eth2.forwarding all set to 1 (cmd-e6159447862b42c5), persisted to /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb-forwarding.conf (cmd-a7a6df50d99b446f), and confirmed still set to 1 after node1 reboot (cmd-054b9bc895bd4458).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are configured with routes to reach the opposite host's subnet via node1
requirements.summary: node2 route to 192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.1 and node3 route to 192.168.10.0/24 via 192.168.20.1, applied live and persisted in /etc/systemd/network/10-enp8s0.network, confirmed present after networkctl reload/reconfigure and after each node's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across the VLAN boundary through node1
requirements.summary: Bidirectional pings between 192.168.10.2 (node2) and 192.168.20.2 (node3) succeed with 0% loss and TTL=63, directly confirming traffic transits node1's router hop. Confirmed both immediately after configuration and again after the full reboot cycle of all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Configuration survives node restarts (interface addressing, forwarding, routes)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baselines with boot_id were captured for all three nodes, each node was rebooted (acknowledged, went unreachable, returned with a new boot_id), and post-restart checks show eth1/eth2 addressing and forwarding sysctls restored on node1 and static addresses/routes restored on node2/node3, with cross-VLAN ping fully working again (0% loss) after all three reboots completed. One transient check immediately after node1's own reboot (cmd-6fe4c1daa86a4753) showed 33% loss (2/3 packets), consistent with brief post-reboot settling rather than a persistent failure, since later checks after all reboots show 0% loss.

overall_summary: The executor correctly identified the VLAN pairing (node1 eth1<->node2, eth2<->node3), addressed node1's routed interfaces, enabled and persisted IPv4 forwarding, added and persisted static routes on node2/node3, and demonstrated bidirectional cross-VLAN reachability with TTL=63 confirming routing through node1. All five material outcomes are satisfied with direct command evidence. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed for all three nodes with pre-restart boot-identity/health baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed post-restart boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and recovered addressing/forwarding/routing/cross-VLAN connectivity, giving strong confidence in both the routing solution and its persistence. One minor, bounded, and effectively self-reverted mutation unrelated to the task (docker0 address removal) slightly lowers the hygiene score.
limitations: A brief 33% packet-loss reading was observed on node2's ping to node3 immediately after node1's reboot (cmd-6fe4c1daa86a4753); this is not treated as a persistent failure since subsequent checks after all reboots show 0% loss, but the trace does not fully explain the transient loss.

The docker0 interface mutation on node1 (cmd-18731b7f5e0c449a) has no stated rationale in the executor's action log; its effective reversal after reboot is inferred from the after-reboot snapshot rather than an explicit restoration step.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, static routes, and their persistence files, plus the mandated reboot/verification cycle for all three nodes. One mutation, cmd-18731b7f5e0c449a on node1 (deleting the 240.127.1.1/24 address from docker0 and setting docker0 down), has no clear connection to the VLAN-routing task or to any prerequisite for it — it appears to be unrelated interface cleanup/troubleshooting. It was bounded and low-risk, and it was not persisted: the after-reboot check (cmd-054b9bc895bd4458) shows docker0 automatically reacquired the 240.127.1.1/24 address, meaning the mutation was implicitly reverted by the reboot rather than deliberately restored by the executor. No other unnecessary, destructive, or unreverted mutations were observed; failed-services and package-health snapshots are unchanged (pre-existing SONiC service-health/watchdog failures, not executor-caused) between after-prepare and after-executor.
